## Purpose and scope

This protocol measures the purity (NanoDrop) and the concentration (Qubit, PicoGreen) of DNA extracts and PCR products. NanoDrop gives absorbance ratios (A~260~/A~280~, A~260~/A~230~); Qubit (single tubes) and PicoGreen (96-well plates) measure double-stranded DNA by fluorescence and are used for concentrations. It applies to DNA extracts from EnGeL-MOLB-DNA-MAG, -DNA-COL, -DNA-BARC and -DNA-BEE, and to PCR products and libraries in EnGeL-MOLB-MB. RNA quantification is not covered [TO CONFIRM: add RNA, or keep in EnGeL-MOLB-RNA].

## Principle

Spectrophotometry measures the absorbance of the sample at 230, 260 and 280 nm; the ratios indicate contamination by protein or by salts and organic compounds. Fluorometry uses dyes that fluoresce only when bound to double-stranded DNA: the signal is compared with standards of known concentration (two standards for Qubit; a lambda DNA dilution series for PicoGreen), so the result is specific to dsDNA.

## Reagent preparation

**PicoGreen**

- **1X TE:** dilute 20X TE 1:20 in nuclease-free water (e.g. 2.5 mL 20X TE + 47.5 mL water for 50 mL).
- **Lambda working stock (2 ng/µL = 2 µg/mL):** dilute the 100 µg/mL lambda DNA 50-fold in 1X TE, e.g. 10 µL Lambda DNA + 490 µL 1X TE for 500 µL (the earlier lab version, 9 µL + 441 µL, gives 450 µL at the same concentration).
- **PicoGreen working reagent:** dilute 1:200 in 1X TE, fresh on the day, in the dark. Per 96-well plate, prepare 5 mL: 25 µL PicoGreen + 4 975 µL 1X TE (50 µL per well).

**PicoGreen standard curve (in duplicate)**

<!-- bench -->
**PicoGreen standards.**

| Standard | Lambda working stock (µL) | 1X TE (µL) | Working reagent (µL) | Concentration (ng/mL) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| S1 | 50 | 0 | 50 | 1000 |
| S2 | 5 | 45 | 50 | 100 |
| S3 | 0.5 | 49.5 | 50 | 10 |
| Blank | 0 | 50 | 50 | 0 |

## Procedure

### Before starting

- Use filter tips at all steps.
- Equilibrate kits to room temperature as required by the kit instructions [TO CONFIRM].

### A. Purity: NanoDrop

(@) Turn on the NanoDrop and let the initialisation run normally.
(@) Clean the pedestal with 7 µL nuclease-free water.
(@) Select the dsDNA program.
(@) Load 1.5 µL of blank (the last reagent used in the extraction protocol), close the pedestal to measure it, then clean it.
(@) Load 1.5 µL of sample, close the pedestal to measure it, then clean it. Repeat for each sample.
(@) After all measurements, clean the pedestal with 7 µL nuclease-free water.

### B. Concentration, single samples: Qubit dsDNA HS

(@) Prepare the two standards in Qubit assay tubes: 190 µL working solution + 10 µL DNA standard #1; 190 µL working solution + 10 µL DNA standard #2.
(@) For each sample, prepare a Qubit assay tube with 199 µL working solution + 1 µL sample.
(@) Vortex vigorously for 3–5 s without creating bubbles.
(@) Incubate all tubes at room temperature for 2 min.
(@) On the Home screen, touch *dsDNA*, select *dsDNA High Sensitivity* and touch *Read standards*.
(@) Insert Standard #1, close the lid and touch *Read standard*; when the reading is complete (c. 3 s), remove it. Repeat with Standard #2.
(@) Touch *Run samples*, select the sample volume (1 µL) and the output units.
(@) Insert each sample tube, close the lid and select *Read tube*; remove the tube when the reading is complete (c. 3 s). Repeat for all samples.

### C. Concentration, 96-well plates: PicoGreen

(@) Pipette each standard into the black plate in duplicate (table in Reagent preparation).
(@) Samples: 2 µL sample + 48 µL 1X TE per well + 50 µL working reagent.
(@) Mix by pipetting or a short plate shake.
(@) Incubate for 2 min at room temperature, protected from light.
(@) Plate reader: *Manage Protocol* → “PicoGREEN_LC_100”; *Start measurement* → *Gain Adjustment*; then *Start measurement*. The reader protocol is a fluorescence-intensity endpoint read (Greiner 96 F-bottom plate; excitation filter 485-12, emission filter 520; top optic; 30 flashes per well; settling time 0.5 s). The gain is set at 80–90% of the highest standard (1 000 ng/mL), and the blank is subtracted in the evaluation.
(@) In the reader software, fit a linear regression of the standards (S1–S3 and blank) (*Calculation* → *Standard curve calculations* → *Linear regression fit*); then, in *Microplate View*, select *Linear Regression Fit* under *Recalculate concentration*.

### After finishing

{{< include ../../includes/_before-you-leave.qmd >}}

## Calculations

**PicoGreen: sample concentration**

$$c_\mathrm{sample} = \frac{c_\mathrm{well} \times 50}{1000}$$

- $c_\mathrm{sample}$: concentration of the sample (ng/µL)
- $c_\mathrm{well}$: concentration read from the standard curve (ng/mL)
- 50: dilution of the sample in the well (2 µL in 100 µL; dimensionless)
- 1000: conversion from ng/mL to ng/µL

**Worked example** (illustrative value): a well reads 400 ng/mL → 400 × 50 / 1000 = 20 ng/µL.

## Quality control

| Control | Purpose | Acceptance criterion |
|:--|:--|:--|
| NanoDrop blank | Zero on the sample matrix | Measured before the samples |
| Qubit standards #1 and #2 | Calibration | [TO CONFIRM] |
| PicoGreen standard curve (S1–S3 + blank, in duplicate) | Calibration | R² ≥ 0.99 |
| DNA purity (A~260~/A~280~, A~260~/A~230~) | Protein, salt or organic carry-over | Ideal: A~260~/A~280~ 1.8–2.0 and A~260~/A~230~ 2.0–2.2. Values outside are flagged, not failed: the PCR decides |
| DNA concentration of extracts | Enough DNA for PCR | General rule: ≥ 10 ng/µL success; < 5 ng/µL fail; depends on the starting quantity and parent material; between 5 and 10 ng/µL the PCR result decides |

The PCR is the best way to evaluate whether the DNA in a sample is viable.

## Data and metadata

- **Outputs:** NanoDrop ratios and concentrations; Qubit or PicoGreen concentrations (ng/µL); plate-reader export.
- **Where:** the *Sample_Tracking* sheet of the Metabarcoding Lab Pipeline workbook (DNA_ngul, A260/280, A260/230) or the project's records, and the lab book; instrument use in the QC equipment user log.

::: {.callout-note title="Minimum to record"}
- EnGeL sample label; date; operator; instrument (NanoDrop / Qubit / plate reader)
- Kit lot numbers (Qubit dsDNA HS, PicoGreen)
- A~260~/A~280~, A~260~/A~230~, concentration (ng/µL) and the method used
- PicoGreen: standard curve R²
:::

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| PicoGreen standard curve R² < 0.99 | Pipetting error in the standards | Prepare the standards again; [TO CONFIRM] |
| Low PicoGreen signal | Reagent exposed to light, or glass tubes used | Prepare the working reagent fresh, in the dark, in plastic tubes. |
| NanoDrop reading unstable | Dirty pedestal | Clean the pedestal with nuclease-free water between samples. |

## Remarks

NanoDrop concentrations include RNA and free nucleotides; use Qubit or PicoGreen for dsDNA concentrations.

PicoGreen: the manual uses a 200 µL assay (100 µL sample + 100 µL working reagent); the lab uses half volumes (100 µL), with the same high-range standards (1 µg/mL, 100 ng/mL, 10 ng/mL, blank). For very dilute samples the manual gives a low-range curve (25 ng/mL to 250 pg/mL).
